```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
echo = TRUE,

```
```{r load_packages}
if (!requireNamespace("pheatmap", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pheatmap")
library(pheatmap)
```
Section 1. Retrieval of primary tumor RNA-seq data (TCGA)

To begin our tumor-level codon analysis, we are retrieving transcript abundance
estimates derived from RNA-seq data generated across a variety of primary human
tumors, as measured by the Cancer Genome Atlas. The values represent normalized
gene expression estimates quantified using RSEM. Because the data are summarized
at the gene level with no transcript ID information, we will select one
representative CDS per gene from Ensembl (see Section 2).
```{r retrieve_tcga}
tcga <- readRDS(url("https://github.com/kvbortle/MCB290_VanBortleLab_Undergraduate_Projects/raw/refs/heads/main/data/TCGA_RNASeq_ATACmatch_RSEM.RDS"))
head(tcga)
cat("Number of genes in TCGA data:", nrow(tcga), "
")
cat("Number of tumor samples: ", ncol(tcga) - 1, "
")
```
Section 2. Build a reference codon key for Ensembl transcripts

Because the TCGA data is gene-level, we pick one representative transcript
per gene: the longest CDS. The longest CDS typically encodes the most complete
protein and is the most biologically relevant isoform. The trade-off is that
isoform switching across tumor types is ignored.
For each representative CDS we:
Split the sequence into non-overlapping triplets (codons)
Count occurrences of each of the 64 possible codons
Store results in a gene × codon count matrix
```{r retrieve_ensembl}
cds <- readRDS("updated_CDS.RDS")
head(cds)
```
```{r build_codon_key}
── 2a. Select longest CDS per gene ──────────────────────────────────────────

cds$cds_length <- nchar(cds$CDS)
cds_rep <- cds[order(cds$GeneName, -cds$cds_length), ]
cds_rep <- cds_rep[!duplicated(cds_rep$GeneName), ]
cat("Representative transcripts selected:", nrow(cds_rep), "
")
── 2b. Define all 64 codons ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

bases <- c("A", "T", "C", "G")
all_codons <- sort(as.vector(outer(outer(bases, bases, paste0), bases, paste0)))
cat("Total codons defined:", length(all_codons), "
")
── 2c. Function to count codons in a single CDS string ──────────────────────

count_codons <- function(seq) {
seq <- toupper(seq)
trimmed_len <- floor(nchar(seq) / 3) * 3
seq <- substr(seq, 1, trimmed_len)
starts <- seq(1, trimmed_len - 2, by = 3)
triplets <- substring(seq, starts, starts + 2)
counts <- table(factor(triplets, levels = all_codons))
return(as.integer(counts))
}
── 2d. Build gene x codon count matrix ──────────────────────────────────────

cat("Computing per-gene codon counts (this may take ~30-60 seconds)...
")
codon_counts_list <- lapply(cds_rep$CDS, count_codons)
codon_count_mat <- do.call(rbind, codon_counts_list)
rownames(codon_count_mat) <- cds_rep$GeneName
colnames(codon_count_mat) <- all_codons
cat("Codon count matrix dimensions:", dim(codon_count_mat), "
")
stopifnot(all(rowSums(codon_count_mat) > 0))
cat("Sanity check passed: all genes have at least one codon.
")
```
Section 3. Determine codon frequency (%) across each tumor type

Using the RSEM values from Section 1 and the codon key from Section 2, we
compute expression-weighted codon frequencies for each sample, then average
within each TCGA tumor type.
Strategy:
Align genes shared between TCGA and the codon key
Use matrix multiplication to compute expression-weighted codon sums per sample
Normalize to frequencies (%) per sample
Aggregate per-sample frequencies to per-tumor-type means
```{r calculate_tumor_codon_freqs}
── 3a. Align genes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

common_genes <- intersect(tcga$gene, rownames(codon_count_mat))
cat("Genes in TCGA: ", nrow(tcga), "
")
cat("Genes in codon key: ", nrow(codon_count_mat), "
")
cat("Genes in common: ", length(common_genes), "
")
expr_mat <- as.matrix(tcga[match(common_genes, tcga$gene), -1])
rownames(expr_mat) <- common_genes
codon_mat <- codon_count_mat[common_genes, ]
── 3b. Expression-weighted codon counts per sample ───────────────────────────

t(expr_mat) is (samples x genes); x codon_mat (genes x codons)

= (samples x 64 codons) weighted codon sums

cat("Computing expression-weighted codon sums...
")
weighted_codon_counts <- t(expr_mat) %% codon_mat
cat("Weighted count matrix dimensions:", dim(weighted_codon_counts), "
")
── 3c. Convert to frequencies (%) ───────────────────────────────────────────

sample_totals <- rowSums(weighted_codon_counts)
codon_freq_samples <- sweep(weighted_codon_counts, 1, sample_totals, "/") * 100
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(codon_freq_samples) - 100) < 1e-6))
cat("Sanity check passed: per-sample frequencies sum to 100%.
")
── 3d. Aggregate by tumor type ───────────────────────────────────────────────

sample_names <- rownames(codon_freq_samples)
tumor_type <- sub("_.", "", sample_names)
tumor_types_unique <- sort(unique(tumor_type))
cat("Tumor types and sample counts:
")
print(table(tumor_type))
tumor_codon_freqs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tumor_types_unique, function(tt) {
idx <- which(tumor_type == tt)
if (length(idx) == 1) codon_freq_samples[idx, ] else colMeans(codon_freq_samples[idx, ])
}))
rownames(tumor_codon_freqs) <- tumor_types_unique
cat("
Final tumor codon frequency matrix:", dim(tumor_codon_freqs), "
")
cat(" rows = tumor types, columns = 64 codons
")
round(tumor_codon_freqs[1:5, 1:8], 4)
```
Section 4. Visualization and comparison

Visualization 1: Tumor vs. normal tissue references

Average codon frequencies across all tumor types are plotted against Shane's
and Madelyn's normal-tissue references. Points near the diagonal indicate tumor
codon usage closely resembles normal tissue; deviations indicate tumor-specific
shifts.
```{r viz1_scatter, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
mean_tumor_freqs <- colMeans(tumor_codon_freqs)
shared_codons <- intersect(names(mean_tumor_freqs), colnames(shane))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
plot(
colMeans(shane[, shared_codons]),
mean_tumor_freqs[shared_codons],
xlab = "Shane — Normal Tissue Codon Freq (%)",
ylab = "This Study — Tumor Codon Freq (%)",
main = "Tumor vs. Normal Tissue
(Shane reference)",
pch = 19, cex = 0.8, col = "#E74C3C"
)
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
r_shane <- round(cor(colMeans(shane[, shared_codons]),
mean_tumor_freqs[shared_codons]), 3)
legend("topleft", bty = "n", legend = paste0("r = ", r_shane))
plot(
colMeans(madelyn[, shared_codons]),
mean_tumor_freqs[shared_codons],
xlab = "Madelyn — Normal Tissue Codon Freq (%)",
ylab = "This Study — Tumor Codon Freq (%)",
main = "Tumor vs. Normal Tissue
(Madelyn reference)",
pch = 19, cex = 0.8, col = "#3498DB"
)
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
r_madelyn <- round(cor(colMeans(madelyn[, shared_codons]),
mean_tumor_freqs[shared_codons]), 3)
legend("topleft", bty = "n", legend = paste0("r = ", r_madelyn))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
```
Visualization 2: Heatmap of codon frequencies across tumor types

Codon frequencies are z-scored column-wise so relative enrichment/depletion is
visible regardless of a codon's absolute baseline frequency. Both rows (tumor
types) and columns (codons) are hierarchically clustered, revealing groups of
tumor types with similar codon usage programs.
```{r viz2_heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
freq_z <- scale(tumor_codon_freqs)
heat_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(100)
pheatmap(
freq_z,
color = heat_colors,
clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
clustering_method = "ward.D2",
fontsize_row = 8,
fontsize_col = 6,
main = "Tumor Codon Frequency (z-score)
across TCGA tumor types",
border_color = NA,
angle_col = 45
)
```
Visualization 3: PCA of tumor types by codon frequency profile

PCA reduces the 64-dimensional codon frequency space to 2D. Tumor types that
cluster together share similar overall codon usage programs. Outliers may
reflect unusual transcriptome composition.
```{r viz3_pca, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
pca_res <- prcomp(tumor_codon_freqs, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
pct_var <- round(100 * pca_res$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2), 1)
n_types <- nrow(tumor_codon_freqs)
set.seed(42)
pal <- rainbow(n_types, s = 0.75, v = 0.85)
par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2), xpd = FALSE)
plot(
pca_res$x[, 1], pca_res$x[, 2],
xlab = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "% variance)"),
ylab = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "% variance)"),
main = "PCA of Tumor Types
by Codon Frequency Profile",
pch = 21, bg = pal, cex = 1.8, col = "black"
)
text(pca_res$x[, 1], pca_res$x[, 2],
labels = rownames(tumor_codon_freqs),
cex = 0.6, pos = 3, col = "grey25")
```
Visualization 4: Leucine synonymous codon usage across tumor types

Leucine has 6 synonymous codons (TTA, TTG, CTT, CTC, CTA, CTG). Within each
sample we compute what fraction of all Leu codons is accounted for by CTG.
Variation across tumor types reflects differences in tRNA availability and
translational efficiency.
```{r viz4_leu_boxplot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
leu_codons <- intersect(c("TTA", "TTG", "CTT", "CTC", "CTA", "CTG"),
colnames(codon_freq_samples))
leu_data <- codon_freq_samples[, leu_codons]
leu_row_totals <- rowSums(leu_data)
leu_rscu <- sweep(leu_data, 1, leu_row_totals, "/") * 100
ctg_vals <- leu_rscu[, "CTG"]
ctg_by_tumor <- split(ctg_vals, sub("_.", "", names(ctg_vals)))
med_order <- names(sort(sapply(ctg_by_tumor, median, na.rm = TRUE)))
ctg_ordered <- ctg_by_tumor[med_order]
par(mar = c(6, 5, 4, 2))
boxplot(
ctg_ordered,
las = 2,
col = "#3498DB",
border = "grey30",
ylab = "CTG as % of all Leu codons",
main = "Leucine CTG Synonymous Codon Usage
across TCGA Tumor Types (ordered by median)",
cex.axis = 0.65,
outline = FALSE
)
abline(h = mean(ctg_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
lty = 2, col = "#E74C3C", lwd = 1.5)
legend("topleft", legend = "Overall mean",
lty = 2, col = "#E74C3C", lwd = 1.5,
bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
```
Visualization 5: Tumor vs. normal tissue codon frequency differences

For each codon we compute: mean tumor frequency − mean normal tissue frequency
(Shane reference). Red bars indicate codons enriched in tumors; blue bars
indicate codons depleted relative to normal tissue.
```{r viz5_delta_barplot, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
tissue_mean <- colMeans(shane[, shared_codons])
tumor_mean <- mean_tumor_freqs[shared_codons]
delta <- tumor_mean - tissue_mean
delta_sorted <- sort(delta, decreasing = TRUE)
par(mar = c(7, 5, 4, 2))
barplot(
delta_sorted,
las = 2,
col = ifelse(delta_sorted > 0, "#E74C3C", "#3498DB"),
ylab = "Δ Codon Frequency (Tumor − Normal, %)",
main = "Tumor vs. Normal Tissue Codon Frequency Differences
(red = enriched in tumors, blue = depleted)",
cex.names = 0.6,
border = NA
)
abline(h = 0, col = "black", lwd = 1)
par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
cat("
Top 5 codons ENRICHED in tumors vs. normal tissue:
")
print(round(head(delta_sorted, 5), 4))
cat("
Top 5 codons DEPLETED in tumors vs. normal tissue:
")
print(round(tail(delta_sorted, 5), 4))
```
